obligations.note: The change sets the Payments privileged idle timeout to 16 in policy.py and policy-params.json, above the catalog's base-commit bound of <= 15. The control test passes only because it compares against the edited policy-params value. No in-scope exception covers the deviation.

EXC-0225 is approved by a risk owner (Vasquez), unexpired at review time and records a compensating control, but it is scoped to component payments.session. The deviation is in payments.policy (policy.py) and payments.controls-data (policy-params.json), and session.py is unchanged, so the exception is out of scope.
Ticket CHG-25247 was approved by change manager erik.brandt on 2026-10-20, before review. Its components (payments.policy, payments.controls-data) cover both changed paths.
Code review approval comes from mara.costa, a Payments change_approver who is a different person from the author jonah.weiss.
Both approvals name head commit e31bae6, and that is the change's only commit.

The CI run on head e31bae6 succeeded with 172 tests, 0 failures and 0 skipped, including the SES-1 exhaustive control test test_privileged_idle_timeout_within_policy. I could not re-run it locally because pytest is not installed.
The touched components (payments.policy, payments.controls-data) are not marked security_sensitive, so no security_review approval is required.
The change alters a protected controls file (policy-params.json). bao.tran, a control_owner in controls-office outside the author's payments-eng team, approved head e31bae6.
The ticket type is standard and the change is not marked emergency, so no PIR is required.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers policy.py or policy-params.json (the entries cover payments.py, audit.py, routes.py and Mortgage files), so no accepted evidence lapses.

summary: The change raises Payments' privileged-session idle timeout from 15 to 16 minutes, breaching SES-1's approved bound of <= 15 minutes. The exhaustive control test passes only because the change also raised the approved value in policy-params.json, which the test compares against. The cited exception EXC-0225 is otherwise valid but is scoped to component payments.session, while the changed code and data are in payments.policy and payments.controls-data, so EXC-1 does not let the deviation stand. The process records (ticket, independent code review, control-owner approval, CI on head) are in order, but the uncovered SES-1 violation requires rejection.
